key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 nanocrystal absorbers with efficient charge extraction, supporting stable near-infrared sub-cells for tandem photovoltaics.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals addresses thickness-limited near-infrared absorption and offers a potentially scalable route to tandem devices.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to passivate nanocrystals and increase film thickness by an order of magnitude.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months in dry air without encapsulation; triple-junction efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
